items.title: Flow calculus of a self-adjoint generator: commutation, invariance and differentiability
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and functional-calculus suppliers. Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $T$ be self-adjoint on $H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) with spectral projection-valued measure $E$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and put
$$U(t):=e^{itT}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R)$$
in the sense of the integral of a measurable function against a projection-valued measure ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]). Then:

(a) $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]) with $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ for all $s,t$; moreover $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$, $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and the difference quotient $\frac1t\bigl(U(t)x-x\bigr)$ has a norm limit as $t\to0$ exactly for $x\in D(T)$, where that limit is $iTx$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]).

(b) For every bounded Borel function $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$ one has $h(T)U(t)=U(t)h(T)$; in particular $E(B)U(t)=U(t)E(B)$ for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$.

(c) For $x\in D(T)$ the map $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t\in\mathbb R$, with
$$\frac{d}{dt}U(t)x=iU(t)Tx=iTU(t)x;$$
for $x\in H\setminus D(T)$ the map $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at no point of $\mathbb R$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]); a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]); a self-adjoint operator $T$ on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]); the operator $U(t)=\int e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); a bounded Borel function $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$; vectors $x\in H$ and real $s,t$.

[F1] **Generated group and generator.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]) with $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$, $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and the difference quotient $\frac1t(U(t)x-x)$ converges as $t\to0$ exactly for $x\in D(T)$, the limit then being $iTx$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]); by [[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]] this says that the generator of $U$ is $iT$ with domain $D(T)$.

[F2] **Bounded Borel calculus.** For bounded Borel $f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ the operator $\Phi_E(f)=\int f\,dE$ is the unique bounded operator with $\langle\Phi_E(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}$ for all $x,y\in H$, obtained as the norm limit of integrals of simple functions along uniform approximations; and $\Phi_E(fg)=\Phi_E(f)\Phi_E(g)$, $\Phi_E(\overline f)=\Phi_E(f)^{*}$, $\Phi_E(\mathbf 1_{\mathbb R})=I$ ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], [[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]], [[thm-pvm-integral-is-a-star-homomorphism]]).

[F3] **The flow as a function of $T$.** $U(t)=\Phi_E(f_t)$ with $f_t(\lambda)=e^{it\lambda}$, and $E(B)=\Phi_E(\mathbf 1_B)$ for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the group properties and the domain characterization from the cited generation lemma, then prove the commutation with the bounded calculus and the everywhere-differentiability statements.

**Given:** A self-adjoint $T$ with spectral PVM $E$; $U(t)=e^{itT}$; a bounded Borel $h$; $x\in H$; $s,t\in\mathbb R$.

1.1 Clause (a) is exactly the statement of the cited generation lemma, read in the notation $U(t)=e^{itT}$: it gives the group law, unitarity, $U(t)^{*}=U(-t)$, the invariance $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$, the commutation $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and the characterization of the difference quotient with limit $iTx$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]). [given, F1]

1.2 For bounded Borel $h$ and fixed $t$, [F2] and [F3] give $h(T)U(t)=\Phi_E(h)\Phi_E(f_t)=\Phi_E(hf_t)$, and multiplication of complex functions is commutative, so $\Phi_E(hf_t)=\Phi_E(f_th)=\Phi_E(f_t)\Phi_E(h)=U(t)h(T)$; this is the first assertion of (b). [given, F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 Let $x\in D(T)$. At $t=0$ the difference quotient converges to $iTx$ by [F1]. For fixed $t$ and $s\to0$ the group law gives $U(t+s)x-U(t)x=U(t)\bigl(U(s)x-x\bigr)$, hence $\frac1s\bigl(U(t+s)x-U(t)x\bigr)=U(t)\frac1s\bigl(U(s)x-x\bigr)\to U(t)iTx=iU(t)Tx$, because $U(t)$ is bounded and the limit in the last factor exists; the identity $iU(t)Tx=iTU(t)x$ is the commutation in [F1]. The derivative $t\mapsto iU(t)Tx$ is continuous because $U$ is strongly continuous and $U(t)Tx$ depends continuously on $t$; hence $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t$ with the displayed derivative. [given, F1, algebra]

1.4 Let $x\in H\setminus D(T)$ and suppose that $t\mapsto U(t)x$ were differentiable at some $t_0$ with derivative $y$. Then for $s\to0$, using the group law and boundedness of $U(-t_0)$, $\frac1s\bigl(U(s)x-x\bigr)=U(-t_0)\frac1s\bigl(U(t_0+s)x-U(t_0)x\bigr)\to U(-t_0)y$, so the difference quotient at $0$ would converge, contradicting [F1], which says that it converges exactly for $x\in D(T)$. Hence $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at no point of $\mathbb R$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Taking $h=\mathbf 1_B$ for a Borel set $B$ in step 1.2 and using $E(B)=\Phi_E(\mathbf 1_B)$ from [F3] gives $E(B)U(t)=U(t)E(B)$, the second assertion of (b). [step 1.2, F3]

3.1 Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 1.3 and 1.4 establish clauses (a), (b) and (c). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 1.4] ∎

## Remarks

- **Sign and scaling conventions.** The physical reading of this lemma uses $T=-K/\hbar$ for a self-adjoint energy operator $K$ and a positive constant $\hbar$; then $D(T)=D(K)$ and $U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}$ in the spectral calculus, while the derivative statement of clause (c) becomes $i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}U(t)x=KU(t)x$ for $x\in D(K)$. The identification of the group generated by $-iK/\hbar$ with the spectral-calculus exponential is the uniqueness statement of Stone's theorem; it is used, not reproved, on the physics pages.
- **Only the domain carries the equation.** Clause (c) shows that the norm-differentiability of the flow is equivalent to membership in $D(T)$; the flow itself, clause (a), is defined on all of $H$ and is continuous there.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (a self-adjoint operator generates a strongly continuous unitary group; the derivative exists exactly on the domain and equals iT)
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.1-2.3, printed pages 10-17 (unitary time evolution, the evolution operator and the generator equation)

items.title: Heisenberg flow of a bounded operator: conjugates, covariance and the equation of motion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $T$ be self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and $U(t)=e^{itT}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]]; for $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) put
$$A(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
Then:

(a) $A(t)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with $A(0)=A$, $\|A(t)\|=\|A\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]) and $A(t)^{*}=A^{*}(t)$; in particular $A$ self-adjoint implies every $A(t)$ self-adjoint ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Moreover $A(t+s)=U(s)^{*}A(t)U(s)$ for all $s,t$.

(b) If $A\,D(T)\subseteq D(T)$, then $A(t)D(T)\subseteq D(T)$ for every $t$, and for every $x\in D(T)$ the map $t\mapsto A(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}A(t)x=-i\,[T,A(t)]x=-i\bigl(TA(t)-A(t)T\bigr)x .$$

(c) For every $x\in H$ the map $t\mapsto A(t)x$ is continuous, and the uniform operator norm bound $\|A(t)\|\le\|A\|$ holds.

(d) If $A$ is self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]), then every $A(t)$ is self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure
$$E_{A(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
and the spectra agree, $\sigma(A(t))=\sigma(A)$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; a self-adjoint operator $T$ with flow $U(t)=e^{itT}$; a bounded operator $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; vectors $x\in H$; real $s,t$.

[F1] **Flow calculus.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with $U(t)^{*}=U(-t)$, $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$, $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and for bounded Borel $h$ one has $h(T)U(t)=U(t)h(T)$; for $x\in D(T)$ the map $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable with derivative $iU(t)Tx$ ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)-(c)).

[F2] **Adjoints and norms.** For $B,C,D\in\mathcal B(H)$ one has $(BCD)^{*}=D^{*}C^{*}B^{*}$, $\|BCD\|\le\|B\|\,\|C\|\,\|D\|$ and $\|B^{*}\|=\|B\|$; each $U(t)$ is unitary, so $\|U(-t)BU(t)\|=\|B\|$ and $U(t)^{*}=U(-t)$ ([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]], [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], [[def-operator-norm]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]).

[F3] **Bounded calculus under unitary conjugation.** Let $E$ be a PVM on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ of a self-adjoint operator and $W$ unitary. Then $B\mapsto WE(B)W^{*}$ is a regular PVM whose scalar measure in $x$ is $E_{W^{*}x}$, and for bounded Borel $f$ one has $\Phi_{WE(\cdot)W^{*}}(f)=W\Phi_E(f)W^{*}$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], [[thm-pvm-integral-is-a-star-homomorphism]]).

[F4] **Truncation definition and uniqueness.** For a PVM $E$ and measurable $f$ one has $f(E)x=\lim_{n}\Phi_E\bigl(f\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}}\bigr)x$ for $x\in D(f(E))$; for bounded self-adjoint operators the representing regular PVM is unique ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]], [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; conjugate the flow properties of [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] by bounded operators, with the product-domain hypothesis used only where the differential equation is asserted.

**Given:** The data of the statement, and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Boundedness, norm and adjoint] $A(t)=U(-t)AU(t)$ is a product of bounded operators, so bounded, and $A(0)=A$; by [F2], $\|A(t)\|=\|A\|$ and $A(t)^{*}=U(t)^{*}A^{*}U(-t)^{*}=U(-t)A^{*}U(t)=A^{*}(t)$; hence $A$ self-adjoint implies $A(t)$ self-adjoint. For the covariance, $A(t+s)=U(-t-s)AU(t+s)=U(s)^{*}U(-t)AU(t)U(s)=U(s)^{*}A(t)U(s)$ by the group law. This is (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Time-invariance of the product-domain hypothesis] Assume $A\,D(T)\subseteq D(T)$. For $y\in D(T)$ one has $U(t)y\in D(T)$ by [F1], then $AU(t)y\in D(T)$ by hypothesis, and finally $U(-t)AU(t)y\in D(T)$ by [F1] again; thus $A(t)y=U(-t)AU(t)y\in D(T)$. [given, F1]

1.3 [Conjugation of the spectral measure] Assume $A$ self-adjoint with spectral PVM $E_A$. Fix $t$ and put $E'(B):=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$. Then $E'$ is a PVM: each $E'(B)$ is an orthogonal projection because $U(-t)=U(t)^{*}$ is unitary and $E_A(B)$ is an orthogonal projection; $E'(\varnothing)=0$, $E'(\mathbb R)=I$; and for pairwise disjoint Borel $B_n$ with union $B$, the strong countable additivity of $E_A$ gives $\sum_nE'(B_n)x=U(-t)\bigl(\sum_nE_A(B_n)U(t)x\bigr)\to U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)x=E'(B)x$ because $U(-t)$ is bounded. It is regular because its scalar measure in $x$ is $E'_x(B)=\|E'(B)x\|^{2}=\langle U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)x,x\rangle=\langle E_A(B)U(t)x,U(t)x\rangle=E_{A,U(t)x}(B)$, a regular Borel measure. [given, F1, F3, F4]

2.1 [Strong continuity] For $x\in H$, $A(t)x-A(s)x=U(-t)A\bigl(U(t)-U(s)\bigr)x+\bigl(U(-t)-U(-s)\bigr)AU(s)x$, and both terms tend to $0$ as $t\to s$ because $U$ is strongly continuous and $A$ is bounded; the norm bound is step 1.1. This is (c). [given, step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Equation of motion] Assume $A\,D(T)\subseteq D(T)$ and let $x\in D(T)$. Decompose $A(t+s)x-A(t)x=U(-t-s)A(U(t+s)x-U(t)x)+(U(-t-s)-U(-t))AU(t)x$; the first term divided by $s$ equals $U(-t-s)A\frac1s(U(t+s)x-U(t)x)$, and $\frac1s(U(t+s)x-U(t)x)\to iU(t)Tx$ by [F1], so it tends to $iU(-t)AU(t)Tx=iA(t)Tx$. For the second term, $y:=AU(t)x$ lies in $D(T)$ by step 1.2, and $\frac1s(U(-s)y-y)\to-iTy$ by [F1] applied at $0$ to the group $s\mapsto U(-s)$; hence the second term divided by $s$ equals $U(-t)\frac1s(U(-s)y-y)\to-iU(-t)Ty=-iTU(-t)y=-iTA(t)x$, using the commutation $TU(-t)=U(-t)T$ on $D(T)$ from [F1]. Adding the two limits gives $\frac{d}{dt}A(t)x=iA(t)Tx-iTA(t)x=-i(TA(t)-A(t)T)x$. This is (b). [given, step 1.2, F1, algebra]

2.3 [Identification as the spectral measure of $A(t)$] With $E'$ as in step 1.3, [F3] gives $\Phi_{E'}(g)=U(-t)\Phi_{E_A}(g)U(t)$ for bounded Borel $g$: the identity holds for indicators by definition of $E'$, extends to simple functions by linearity, and passes to uniform limits by the norm estimate of [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clause 1. Applying the truncation definition [F4] with $g_n(\lambda)=\lambda\mathbf 1_{\{|\lambda|\le n\}}$ and $x\in H$ (the domain is all of $H$ because $A$ is bounded) gives $\int\lambda\,dE'(\lambda)x=\lim_n\Phi_{E'}(g_n)x=\lim_nU(-t)\Phi_{E_A}(g_n)U(t)x=U(-t)(\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda))U(t)x=U(-t)AU(t)x=A(t)x$, where the middle limit is interchanged with the bounded operator $U(-t)$ and $\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)=A$ is the spectral representation of the bounded self-adjoint $A$. Hence $E'$ represents the bounded self-adjoint $A(t)$, and by uniqueness [F4] it is the spectral PVM of $A(t)$. [given, step 1.3, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Spectra] For a self-adjoint operator with spectral PVM $F$, the spectrum consists of the points $\lambda$ with $F((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))\ne0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ ([[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]] clause 4 with $f$ the identity). By step 2.3, $E_{A(t)}((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))=U(-t)E_A((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))U(t)$ is nonzero exactly when $E_A((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))$ is; hence $\sigma(A(t))=\sigma(A)$. [given, step 2.3, F4]

4.1 Steps 1.1, 2.1, 1.2, 2.2, 1.3, 2.3 and 3.1 prove (a)-(d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, step 1.3, step 2.3, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Where the hypothesis is needed.** Clauses (a) and (c) require nothing beyond boundedness of $A$; clause (b), and with it the Heisenberg equation, uses the product-domain hypothesis $A\,D(T)\subseteq D(T)$, which is exactly the condition under which the differentiated products are defined. A bounded observable whose spectral PVM commutes with that of $T$ satisfies the hypothesis trivially, because then $A$ maps every $D(h(T))$ into itself.
- **Transported measurable functional calculus.** Step 2.3 shows more than the statement of (d): for every bounded Borel $g$ the operator $g(A(t))$ equals $U(-t)g(A)U(t)$; this is the operator form of the statement that the unitary flow is an automorphism of the algebra of bounded Borel functions of the observable.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 3.1-3.2, printed pages 18-22 (Heisenberg operators and the Heisenberg equation of motion)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 4.4, printed pages 70-71 (the Heisenberg picture: definition of the time-dependent operator, equation of motion, and equality of expectation values with the Schroedinger picture)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58, and Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (domain invariance and differentiability of the unitary flow)

items.title: Stationary rays of a self-adjoint flow are exactly the eigenrays
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]), let $T$ be self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) with spectral projection-valued measure $E$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), let $U(t)=e^{itT}=\int e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)$ be the generated strongly continuous unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]), and let $\psi\in H$ with $\psi\ne0$. Then the following are equivalent:

(i) for every $t\in\mathbb R$ the vector $U(t)\psi$ is a complex multiple of $\psi$ (the ray of $\psi$ is invariant under the flow);

(ii) $\psi\in D(T)$ and $T\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ (the ray of $\psi$ is an eigenray of $T$).

If these hold for the eigenvalue $\lambda$, then $U(t)\psi=e^{it\lambda}\psi$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; a self-adjoint operator $T$ with spectral PVM $E$ and flow $U(t)=\int e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)$; a nonzero vector $\psi\in H$.

[F1] **Flow and domain.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group, $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$, and for $u\in D(T)$ the difference quotient $\frac1s\bigl(U(s)u-u\bigr)$ converges to $iTu$ as $s\to0$, while for $u\notin D(T)$ it does not converge; moreover $E(B)U(t)=U(t)E(B)$ for every Borel $B$ ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)-(c)).

[F2] **Flow as a bounded function of $T$.** $U(t)=\Phi_E(f_t)$ with $f_t(\lambda)=e^{it\lambda}$, and for $x\in H$ and bounded Borel $g$ one has $\|\Phi_E(g)x\|^{2}=\int|g|^{2}\,dE_x$, where $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clause 2, [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]).

[F3] **Eigenvector identity.** For $u\in D(T)$ and real $\mu$ one has $\|(T-\mu)u\|^{2}=\int(\lambda-\mu)^{2}\,dE_u(\lambda)$ ([[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]).

[F4] **Vanishing criterion.** If $g\ge0$ is measurable with $\int g\,dE_u=0$, then $g=0$ $E_u$-almost everywhere ([[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]]).

[F5] **Closed subspaces and Stone's theorem.** The span $K=\mathbb Cu$ of a nonzero vector is closed ([[cor-finite-dimensional-subspaces-are-closed]]) and, with the restricted inner product, is a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-closed-subspace-of-a-banach-space-is-banach]]); a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on a complex Hilbert space equals $t\mapsto e^{itS}$ for a unique self-adjoint generator $S$, and $D(S)$ is exactly the set of vectors whose difference quotients converge, with limit $iSx$ ([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]], [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

[F6] **Reality of eigenvalues.** A self-adjoint operator is symmetric: $\langle Su,u\rangle=\langle u,Su\rangle$ for every $u\in D(S)$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]); if $Su=\lambda u$ with $u\ne0$ and $u\in D(S)$, then $\lambda\|u\|^{2}=\langle Su,u\rangle=\langle u,Su\rangle=\overline\lambda\,\|u\|^{2}$, so $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; the forward implication reads the spectral measure of an eigenvector, the converse restricts the flow to the closed invariant span of $\psi$ and applies Stone's theorem there.

**Given:** The data of the statement, and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Eigenrays are stationary] Assume (ii): $T\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and set $u:=\psi/\|\psi\|$, so that $Tu=\lambda u$ and $\|u\|=1$. By [F3], $\int(\lambda'-\lambda)^{2}\,dE_u(\lambda')=\|(T-\lambda)u\|^{2}=0$; the integrand is nonnegative and measurable, so by [F4] it vanishes $E_u$-almost everywhere, that is, $E_u(\mathbb R\setminus\{\lambda\})=0$. Fix $t$ and put $g_t(\lambda'):=e^{it\lambda'}-e^{it\lambda}$, a bounded Borel function vanishing $E_u$-almost everywhere; by [F2], $\|U(t)u-e^{it\lambda}u\|^{2}=\|\Phi_E(g_t)u\|^{2}=\int|g_t|^{2}\,dE_u=0$, so $U(t)u=e^{it\lambda}u$ and, multiplying by $\|\psi\|$, $U(t)\psi=e^{it\lambda}\psi$. In particular $U(t)\psi$ is a multiple of $\psi$ for every $t$, which is (i). The reality of $\lambda$ is [F6] applied to the unit vector $u$. [given, F2, F3, F4, F6, algebra]

1.2 [The invariant span] Assume (i). Multiplication by the nonzero scalar $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ shows that $u:=\psi/\|\psi\|$ satisfies $U(t)u=c(t)u$ with $c(t)\in\mathbb C$ for every $t$; since $U(t)$ is unitary and $\|u\|=1$, one has $|c(t)|=1$. By [F5], $K:=\mathbb Cu$ is a closed subspace of $H$ and, with the restricted inner product, a complex Hilbert space; by (i) each $U(t)$ maps $K$ into $K$, and because $U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ also maps $K$ into $K$, the restriction $W(t):=U(t)|_K$ is a bijection of $K$ onto itself. [given, F1, F5, algebra]

2.1 [The restricted group] The maps $W(t)$ are unitary on $K$: they are norm preserving on $K$ because $U(t)$ is, and they are onto $K$ by step 1.2. The group law $W(t+s)=W(t)W(s)$ and the continuity of $t\mapsto W(t)x$ for each $x\in K$ are inherited from $U$. Hence $W$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on the Hilbert space $K$. [given, step 1.2, F1, F5]

3.1 [Generator on the span] By [F5] applied to $W$ on $K$, there is a self-adjoint operator $T_K$ on $K$ with $W(t)=e^{itT_K}$, whose domain $D(T_K)$ consists exactly of the vectors $x\in K$ for which $\frac1s(W(s)x-x)$ converges, the limit then being $iT_Kx$. A self-adjoint operator is densely defined ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), so $D(T_K)$ is a dense subspace of the one-dimensional space $K$; hence $D(T_K)=K$ and $T_Ku=\lambda u$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$. Since $T_K$ is symmetric on $K$ and $u\ne0$, [F6] gives $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. [given, step 2.1, F5, F6]

4.1 [Transfer to the ambient space] By step 3.1 and [F5], the difference quotient $\frac1s\bigl(W(s)u-u\bigr)=\frac1s\bigl(U(s)u-u\bigr)$ converges in $K$, hence in $H$, to $iT_Ku=i\lambda u$. By [F1], the quotient of the ambient flow converges exactly for vectors of $D(T)$, with limit $iT$ applied to the vector; therefore $u\in D(T)$ and $iTu=i\lambda u$, that is, $Tu=\lambda u$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Multiplying by $\|\psi\|$ gives $T\psi=\lambda\psi$ and $\psi\in D(T)$, which is (ii). [given, step 3.1, F1, F5, algebra]

5.1 Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 prove the equivalence and the additional display of the statement. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Normalization is bookkeeping.** The proof normalizes $\psi$ only to use the unit vector in the inner-product computations of [F6] and step 1.1; the statement itself does not require $\|\psi\|=1$.
- **No converse beyond rays.** Clause (i) concerns the invariance of the ray; it does not claim that $U(t)\psi=\psi$ for an eigenvector, because the eigenvalue phase $e^{it\lambda}$ is present. The statement that the two vectors lie in one ray, hence determine the same pure preparation, is the content of the phase-invariance of states, not an equality of vectors.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.1, printed pages 18-20 (Heisenberg operators, conservation and stationary states)

items.title: Assigned energy observable, unitary flow and the two pictures of autonomous evolution
items.statement:
**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

## Remarks

- **Units and dimensionless phases.** The energy unit $u_H$ and $\hbar$ are part of the model's quantity conventions: $H_{\mathrm{op}}t/\hbar$ is a dimensionless spectral variable, and the argument of the exponential is read in those units. No numerical value of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is asserted.
- **Domain matters.** The flow $U(t)$ is defined on all of $H$, while the energy operator and every unbounded assigned observable are defined only on their domains; the Schroedinger equation and the Heisenberg equation are domain-qualified statements and are proved as such on this page.
- **Rays and global phases.** The pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ is a ray, so a common phase of all components of $\psi(t)$ is not part of the physical description; a *relative* phase between components is physical and is what the evolving state changes.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58, and Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (self-adjoint observables, the unitary group they generate and the domain-qualified Schroedinger equation)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.1-3.2, printed pages 10-22 (unitary time evolution, the evolution operator, Heisenberg operators and the Heisenberg equation)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 2.2 and 4.3-4.4, printed pages 21-23 and 68-71 (time evolution, conserved quantities, stationary states and the Heisenberg picture)

items.physical_scope: The evolution vocabulary of the framework's autonomous-dynamics postulate P4: the assigned energy observable and its unit, the unitary flow it generates, the Schroedinger-picture evolution of state vectors and density operators, the Heisenberg-picture representative of a bounded assigned sharp observable, stationarity of pure preparations, and compatibility (conservation) of an assigned sharp observable with the energy. This item fixes readings and terminology of P4 together with P1 and P2; it adopts no assumption beyond those postulates and the cited mathematics, asserts no evolution for driven or open systems, no measurement or apparatus realization, no isolation claim about any laboratory system, and no empirical result.

items.title: The Schroedinger-picture flow: unitarity, domain invariance and the domain-qualified equation
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. Let $H$ be the state space assigned to a declared isolated system of the massive-matter sector ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be its assigned energy observable with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (a)), and let
$$U(t)=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda),\qquad \psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0),\qquad \rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$$
be the flow and the state evolutions of clauses (b) and (c) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], with $\hbar>0$ and the energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) **Unitary flow.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]) with $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$; every orbit has constant norm, $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(0)\|$, so for $\psi(0)\ne0$ the ray $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation of the model for every $t$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

(b) **Domain invariance.** $U(t)D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ for every $t$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)=U(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}$ on $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$: the flow preserves the energy domain and commutes with the energy there.

(c) **Schroedinger equation on the domain.** For $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ is norm-differentiable at every $t\in\mathbb R$, it stays in $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, and
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)\psi(0);$$
for $\psi(0)\in H\setminus D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve is norm-differentiable at no $t\in\mathbb R$, so the equation is not asserted there, although the evolution $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ remains continuous.

(d) **Density-operator evolution.** For every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and every $t$ the operator $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ is again a preparation: self-adjoint, positive, trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Moreover for every bounded operator $B$ the identity $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)B\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)U(t)^{*}BU(t)\bigr)$ holds.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P4 and the cited mathematics. They assert no evolution for a prescribed time-dependent Hamiltonian, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement, apparatus or detector model, no claim that any laboratory system is isolated, and no empirical result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1 and P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]); the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with PVM $E_H$ and flow $U(t)$ of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]; a vector $\psi(0)\in H$; a preparation $\rho$; a bounded operator $B$.

[F1] **P4, read through the definition.** Clause (i) of P4 assigns the energy operator: $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is self-adjoint with a declared energy unit; clause (ii) fixes $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ as the strongly continuous unitary group generated by it, with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ for $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$; clause (iii) fixes $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi(0)$ and $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ and states the Schroedinger equation as holding exactly for initial vectors in $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] clauses (i)-(iii), [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **Flow calculus.** For the self-adjoint $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $U(t)=e^{itT}$: $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$ and $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$; for $u\in D(T)$ the curve $t\mapsto U(t)u$ is differentiable at every $t$ with derivative $iU(t)Tu=iTU(t)u$; for $u\notin D(T)$ it is differentiable at no point ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clauses (a) and (c), [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

[F3] **P1, read through the state-space vocabulary.** Pure preparations are the unit rays of the assigned Hilbert space and general preparations are exactly the states $\rho\in D(H)$: self-adjoint positive trace-class operators with trace one ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clauses (ii)-(iii), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).

[F4] **Trace-class calculus.** The trace-class operators form a two-sided operator ideal, so $U\rho U^{*}$ is trace class for a preparation $\rho$ and a unitary $U$; the trace is linear and cyclic, $\operatorname{tr}(SA)=\operatorname{tr}(AS)$ for trace-class $S$ and bounded $A$ ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]] clause (b)); a self-adjoint operator $B$ is positive exactly when $\langle Bx,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$ ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; translate P4 into the mathematical generator $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$, apply the flow calculus of [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]], and verify the density-operator claims with the trace-class calculus.

**Given:** P1, P4, the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$, its flow $U(t)$, a vector $\psi(0)$, a preparation $\rho$, a bounded operator $B$, and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [The flow and the orbits] Put $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$, a self-adjoint operator with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; by clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] the flow is $U(t)=e^{itT}$. By [F2], $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with the displayed inverse and group laws, and $\|\psi(t)\|=\|U(t)\psi(0)\|=\|\psi(0)\|$ because $U(t)$ is unitary. If $\psi(0)\ne0$ then $\psi(t)\ne0$, and by the normalization clause (ii) of P1 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) the unit ray $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation; this is (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 [Domain invariance] $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(T)$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}=-\hbar T$, so the invariance $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$ and the commutation $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$ of [F2] read as $U(t)D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)=U(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}$ on $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; this is (b). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 [Preparations evolve to preparations] Let $\rho$ be a preparation, so $\rho$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ by [F3]. Then $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}$ is trace class by the ideal property of [F4]. It is self-adjoint because $\rho(t)^{*}=U(t)\rho^{*}U(t)^{*}=\rho(t)$; it is positive because $\langle\rho(t)x,x\rangle=\langle\rho\,U(t)^{*}x,U(t)^{*}x\rangle\ge0$ for every $x$, using positivity of $\rho$ and unitarity of $U(t)$; and its trace is $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=\operatorname{tr}(U(t)\rho U(t)^{*})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho U(t)^{*}U(t))=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, where the second equality is trace cyclicity from [F4] applied to the trace-class operator $\rho U(t)^{*}$ and the bounded operator $U(t)$. Hence $\rho(t)$ is again a preparation. [given, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Schroedinger equation] Let $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(T)$. By [F2] the curve is differentiable at every $t$ with $\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=iU(t)T\psi(0)$, and $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi(0)\in D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ by step 1.2. Substituting $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ and using the commutation of step 1.2 gives $i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=i\hbar\cdot iU(t)T\psi(0)=-\hbar U(t)(-\frac1\hbar H_{\mathrm{op}})\psi(0)=U(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0)=H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)\psi(0)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)$. [given, step 1.2, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Two-picture statistics identity] For bounded $B$, cyclicity from [F4] applied to the trace-class operator $\rho U(t)^{*}B$ and the bounded operator $U(t)$ gives $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)B\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}B\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho U(t)^{*}BU(t)\bigr)$, which is the displayed identity of (d). [given, step 1.3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Outside the domain] If $\psi(0)\in H\setminus D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=H\setminus D(T)$, then by [F2] the curve $t\mapsto U(t)\psi(0)$ is differentiable at no point of $\mathbb R$; this completes (c). [given, step 2.1, F2]

4.1 Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1, 1.3 and 2.2 establish (a)-(d); clause (e) records what the statement does not assert, in agreement with clauses (iv) and (v) of P4. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.3, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Isolated idealization.** P4 is adopted only for an isolated autonomous system; the model equation (c) is a statement about the model's evolution operator, not evidence that a given laboratory system is isolated.
- **No state reduction.** Nothing in this item is a measurement postulate: the evolution $\rho\mapsto U\rho U^{*}$ is applied to a preparation, and no outcome, apparatus or conditioning is introduced.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (the unitary group generated by a self-adjoint operator, invariance of the domain and the domain-qualified Schroedinger equation)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.1-2.2, printed pages 10-15 (unitary time evolution, composition and inverses of the evolution operator, and the Schroedinger equation)
D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted complete lecture set), Section 1.2, printed pages 9-13 (the Schroedinger equation and the conservation of total probability)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the state and composition postulate P1 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 for a declared isolated system of the framework: the flow generated by the assigned energy observable is a strongly continuous unitary group, it preserves the operator domain and commutes with the energy there, the Schroedinger equation holds in the norm-differentiable sense exactly on the domain, and the evolution of a density-operator preparation is a trace-one density operator at every time. The item asserts no dynamics for driven or open systems, no measurement or apparatus realization, no isolation claim about any laboratory system and no empirical result; all statements are conditional on P1 and P4 and on the cited mathematics.

items.title: The Heisenberg picture: equivalent predictions and the domain-qualified equation of motion
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] (P2), and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be the assigned energy observable of a declared isolated system with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ as in [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable: $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ is self-adjoint everywhere defined ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Put
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
Then:

(a) **The Heisenberg representative is an assigned sharp observable.** For every $t$, $A_H(t)$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $\|A_H(t)\|=\|A\|$ and spectrum $\sigma(A_H(t))=\sigma(A)$, and its spectral projection-valued measure is
$$E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel});$$
with the declared unit $u_A$ it is again a bounded assigned sharp observable of the framework, and $A_H(0)=A$.

(b) **The two pictures assign the same laws.** For every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_H(t)}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
where $\mu^{\cdot}_{\cdot}$ is the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$; for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ this reads $\|E_A(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_{A_H(t)}(B)\psi\|^{2}$. In particular the expectation value of the bounded observable agrees, $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)A_H(t)\bigr)$.

(c) **Heisenberg equation.** If $A\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subseteq D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, then for every $x\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve $t\mapsto A_H(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t$ and
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}A_H(t)x=\bigl[A_H(t),H_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr]x=\bigl(A_H(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}-H_{\mathrm{op}}A_H(t)\bigr)x .$$

(d) **Energy-compatible observables are frozen.** If $A$ is compatible with the energy, that is $E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel $B,C$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)), then $A_H(t)=A$ for every $t$, and by (b) the outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is the same in $\rho(t)$ as in $\rho(0)$ for every preparation.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P4 and the cited mathematics. They introduce no new physical assumption, no measurement or apparatus model, no collapse, no driven or open dynamics; they make no claim about which laboratory quantity realizes $(A,u_A)$ and record no empirical result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1, P2, P4; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with flow $U(t)$; a bounded self-adjoint $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$; the representatives $A_H(t)=U(t)^{*}AU(t)$; a preparation $\rho$; a Borel set $B$; a vector $x\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; real $t$.

[F1] **Flow and pictures.** $U$ is the strongly continuous unitary flow of P4(ii); the Schroedinger-picture evolutions are $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi(0)$ and $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$, which is a preparation for every $t$; and for every bounded $B_0$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(t)B_0)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(0)U(t)^{*}B_0U(t))$ ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F2] **Heisenberg flow.** With $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$, the conjugates $A(t)=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=A_H(t)$ satisfy: $A_H(t)$ bounded with $\|A_H(t)\|=\|A\|$ and $A_H(t)^{*}=A_H(t)$; $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$ and $\sigma(A_H(t))=\sigma(A)$; if $A D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subseteq D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ then $\frac{d}{dt}A_H(t)x=-i[T,A_H(t)]x$ for $x\in D(T)$ ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a), (b), (d)).

[F3] **Conserved spectral laws.** Let $K$ be self-adjoint with PVM $E_K$ and $U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}$. If a bounded operator $B_0$ satisfies $B_0E_K(C)=E_K(C)B_0$ for every Borel $C$, then $B_0U(t)=U(t)B_0$ for every $t$; and if a PVM $F$ satisfies $F(S)E_K(C)=E_K(C)F(S)$ for all $S$ in its measurable space and all Borel $C$, then $\operatorname{tr}(U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}F(S))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F(S))$ for every preparation $\rho$ and all $t,S$ ([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conserved-spectral-probability-laws]] clauses (a) and (b)(ii)).

[F4] **Outcome law.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A_0,u_{A_0})$ with spectral PVM $E_{A_0}$, the outcome law of a preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A_0}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A_0}(B))$, equal to $\|E_{A_0}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ for the pure preparation of a unit $\psi$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

[F5] **Spectral uniqueness.** A self-adjoint operator has a unique regular PVM representing it, and two bounded self-adjoint operators with the same spectral PVM are equal ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]; for the bounded case the representing integral is $\Phi_E(\mathrm{id})$).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the mathematical Heisenberg flow at the generator $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$, express the outcome law through the trace identity of the Schroedinger-picture theorem, and read the compatibility statement from the conserved-spectral-law theorem.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Representative and conjugation of the law] By [F2], $A_H(t)$ is bounded, self-adjoint and of norm $\|A\|$, with spectral PVM $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$ and $\sigma(A_H(t))=\sigma(A)$, and $A_H(0)=U(0)^{*}AU(0)=A$; with the declared unit $u_A$ it is an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a). This is (a). [given, F2]

2.1 [Equality of laws] Let $\rho$ be a preparation. By [F4] and [F1], $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)E_A(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)U(t)^{*}E_A(B)U(t)\bigr)$, and by step 1.1 the last expression is $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)E_{A_H(t)}(B)\bigr)$, which equals $\mu^{A_H(t)}_{\rho(0)}(B)$ by [F4]; this is the first display of (b). For the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$, the same chain with $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ gives $\|E_A(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|U(t)E_{A_H(t)}(B)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_{A_H(t)}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, using $E_A(B)U(t)=U(t)E_{A_H(t)}(B)$, which follows from the PVM identity of step 1.1 by multiplying on the left by $U(t)$. [given, step 1.1, F1, F4, algebra]

2.2 [Heisenberg equation] Assume $A\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subseteq D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and let $x\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(T)$ with $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$. By [F2], $\frac{d}{dt}A_H(t)x=-i[T,A_H(t)]x$; substituting $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ gives $\frac{d}{dt}A_H(t)x=\frac{i}{\hbar}\bigl[H_{\mathrm{op}},A_H(t)\bigr]x$, and multiplying by $i\hbar$ gives $i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}A_H(t)x=-\bigl[H_{\mathrm{op}},A_H(t)\bigr]x=\bigl[A_H(t),H_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr]x$, which is the display of (c). [given, step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Expectation identity] Taking $B_0=A$ in the trace identity of [F1] and using $A_H(t)=U(t)^{*}AU(t)$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(t)A)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(0)A_H(t))$, the last assertion of (b). [given, step 2.1, F1, algebra]

3.2 [Frozen energy-compatible observables] Assume $A$ is energy-compatible. For every Borel $B$, the bounded operator $E_A(B)$ commutes with every $E_H(C)$, so [F3] gives $E_A(B)U(t)=U(t)E_A(B)$ for every $t$. Multiplying on the left by $U(t)^{*}=U(-t)$ gives $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)=E_A(B)$ by step 1.1; hence $A_H(t)$ and $A$ have the same spectral PVM and, by [F5], $A_H(t)=A$ for every $t$. With step 2.1 the outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is therefore the same in $\rho(t)$ as in $\rho(0)$; this is (d). [given, step 1.1, step 2.1, F3, F5, algebra]

4.1 Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 2.2 and 3.2 prove (a)-(d); clause (e) records the scope. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, step 3.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **The two pictures are not two theories.** Step 2.1 is an identity between outcome laws, not a derivation of one picture from the other; the Schroedinger picture and the Heisenberg picture are two ways of computing the same numbers $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)$.
- **Domain hypothesis in the equation of motion.** The hypothesis $A\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subseteq D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ in (c) is exactly what makes the differentiated products defined; the position, momentum and other unbounded quantities of later pages are not bounded observables and are not covered by this theorem.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 3.1-3.2, printed pages 18-22 (Heisenberg operators, their properties, and the Heisenberg equation of motion)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 4.4, printed pages 70-71 (the Heisenberg picture: the time-dependent operator, its equation of motion and the equality of expectation values with the Schroedinger picture)
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58 (self-adjoint observables and their spectral measures)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of this page for a declared isolated system: the Heisenberg representative of a bounded assigned sharp observable is again a bounded assigned sharp observable with the same unit, norm and spectrum, the two pictures assign the same outcome laws to every preparation, the domain-qualified Heisenberg equation holds, and energy-compatible bounded observables are frozen in the Heisenberg picture. No measurement, apparatus, detector, driven-dynamics or open-system claim is made, and no empirical result is asserted.

items.title: Energy conservation, conserved sharp observables and the stationary eigenrays
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] (P2), and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be the assigned energy observable of a declared isolated system with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]), and write $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$. Then:

(a) **Energy law and moments.** For every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)E_H(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)E_H(B)\bigr)=\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ likewise $\|E_H(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_H(B)\psi\|^{2}$. If $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, the mean and the second moment of the energy law of $[\psi(0)]$ are finite and time-independent, with time-zero values $\langle H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0),\psi(0)\rangle$ and $\|H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0)\|^{2}$; if one of these moments is infinite at time zero, no equality of finite quantities is claimed.

(b) **Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable that is compatible with the energy ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)). Then its outcome law is time-independent: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B).$$

(c) **Stationary states are exactly the eigenrays.** Let $\psi\in H$, $\psi\ne0$. The pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, that is $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, if and only if $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$: $\psi\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. In that case $\psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi(0)$ for every $t$, and every assigned sharp observable has a time-independent outcome law in this preparation: $\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)$ for every $(A,u_A)$, every Borel $B$ and every $t$.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** No equilibration, relaxation, decay or convergence of the law of an arbitrary preparation is asserted; no moment beyond those finite at time zero is claimed; the converse of (b) — constancy of the law of a bounded observable in every preparation implying strong spectral compatibility with the energy — is not asserted for a general (possibly unbounded) $H_{\mathrm{op}}$; and the item is conditional on the isolated-system idealization of P4, asserting no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1, P2 and P4; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with PVM $E_H$ and flow $U(t)$; a preparation $\rho$; a bounded assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$; a nonzero vector $\psi$; a Borel set $B$; real $t$.

[F1] **Flow and preparation evolution.** $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ is the strongly continuous unitary flow of P4(ii), $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ is a preparation for every $t$, and $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation whenever $\psi(0)\ne0$ ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F2] **Conserved spectral laws.** Let $K$ be self-adjoint with PVM $E_K$ and $U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}$. Then: for every preparation $\rho$ the energy law $\operatorname{tr}(\rho U(t)^{*}E_K(C)U(t))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_K(C))$ is independent of $t$; if $\psi\in D(K)$ the scalar moments $\int\lambda^{k}\,dE_{K,U(t)\psi}$ for $k=1,2$ equal those at time zero, with values $\langle K\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|K\psi\|^{2}$; if a bounded operator $B_0$ commutes with every $E_K(C)$ then $B_0U(t)=U(t)B_0$; if a PVM $F$ commutes with $E_K$ in the strong spectral sense then $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}F(S)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F(S)\bigr)$ for all $t,S$; and a unit eigenvector $K\psi=\lambda\psi$ satisfies $U(t)\psi=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi$ ([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conserved-spectral-probability-laws]] clauses (a), (b)(ii), (c) and (d)).

[F3] **Outcome law and moments.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A_0,u_{A_0})$ the outcome law of a preparation is $\mu^{A_0}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A_0}(B))$, for a unit pure preparation $\|E_{A_0}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, and this number depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; for a unit vector in $D(A_0)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A_0\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A_0\psi\|^{2}$, and they exist exactly under the stated domain hypotheses ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b) and (e)).

[F4] **Stationary-ray characterization.** For a self-adjoint $T$ with flow $U(t)=e^{itT}$ and a nonzero $\psi$, the invariance of the ray, $U(t)\psi\in\mathbb C\psi$ for all $t$, is equivalent to $\psi\in D(T)$ and $T\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some real $\lambda$; and then $U(t)\psi=e^{it\lambda}\psi$ ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-ray-characterization]]).

[F5] **The energy convention.** $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ equals $e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, and the PVM of $K=H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is $E_H$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b), [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the energy law, moments, compatible-observable law and eigenray evolution from the conserved-spectral-law theorem with $K=H_{\mathrm{op}}$, whose convention $U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}$ is exactly the framework's, and prove the converse of the stationarity characterization with the stationary-ray lemma.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Energy law] Instantiate [F2] with $K=H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and its PVM $E_K=E_H$; this is the same flow as [F1] by [F5]. Its first statement gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(0)E_H(B))=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}E_H(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(t)E_H(B))$ for every preparation and every Borel $B$, which is the first display of (a) after reading the outcome law through [F3]; the pure-vector form follows from [F3] with $[\psi(t)]$ and the identity $U(t)^{*}E_H(B)U(t)=E_H(B)$, or directly from the second statement of [F2] with $F=E_H$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

1.2 [Eigenrays are stationary] Let $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\psi\ne0$. The last statement of [F2] with $K=H_{\mathrm{op}}$ gives $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi$ for every $t$; since the scalar $e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}$ is nonzero, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ and $[\psi]$ is stationary. Moreover, for every assigned sharp observable $(A_0,u_{A_0})$ the law $\mu^{A_0}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\|E_{A_0}(B)\psi(t)\|^{2}$ depends only on the ray $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ by [F3], so it equals $\mu^{A_0}_{\psi(0)}(B)$; this is the forward direction and the final assertion of (c). [given, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Moments] If $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(K)$, the moment statement of [F2] with $k=1,2$ gives the displayed time-independence of the two spectral moments, with values $\langle K\psi(0),\psi(0)\rangle=\langle H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0),\psi(0)\rangle$ and $\|K\psi(0)\|^{2}=\|H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0)\|^{2}$, independently of $t$; by [F3] these spectral moments are the mean and the second moment of the energy law, which are therefore finite and time-independent. If a moment is infinite at time zero, the hypothesis of the moment statement fails and no equality is claimed; this completes (a). [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

2.2 [Compatible bounded observables] Let $(A,u_A)$ be bounded and energy-compatible, so $F:=E_A$ satisfies $F(S)E_H(C)=E_H(C)F(S)$ for all Borel $S,C$. The third statement of [F2], with $K=H_{\mathrm{op}}$, gives $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)F(S)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)F(S)\bigr)$ for every $t$ and every Borel $S$; reading $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F(S))$ through [F3] as $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(S)$ gives the display of (b). [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

2.3 [Only eigenrays are stationary] Conversely, let $[\psi]$ be stationary, that is $U(t)\psi\in\mathbb C\psi$ for every $t$, with $\psi\ne0$. By [F5], $U(t)=e^{itT}$ with the self-adjoint $T=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$, $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$. Applying [F4] to $T$ and $\psi$ gives $\psi\in D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and $T\psi=\lambda'\psi$ with $\lambda'\in\mathbb R$; multiplying by $-\hbar$ gives $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\lambda=-\hbar\lambda'\in\mathbb R$. Together with step 1.2 this proves (c). [given, step 1.2, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 Steps 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 1.2 and 2.3 prove (a)-(c); clause (d) records that the statement asserts neither equilibration nor the converse of (b) for unbounded $H_{\mathrm{op}}$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.2, step 2.3] ∎

## Remarks

- **What "conservation of energy" means here.** The conserved object is the outcome law of the assigned energy observable — a probability measure on the Borel sets — and, when they exist, its first two moments. The statement does not say that a single numerical value of the energy is revealed at each time, and it does not identify $\langle H_{\mathrm{op}}\rangle$ with a measured calorimetric energy.
- **Stationarity is a ray statement.** Because the pure law depends only on the ray, the stationary property of an eigenray is stable under the phase $e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}$; a *superposed* preparation of two eigenrays with distinct eigenvalues is generally not stationary, and that failure is exhibited on the companion page.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 2.2.1, printed pages 23-24 (Ehrenfest's theorem, conserved quantities and the conservation of the expectation of the energy)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.1 and 3.2, printed pages 10-17 and 20-22 (norm conservation, Heisenberg operators and operators constant in time when they commute with the Hamiltonian)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of this page for a declared isolated system: the outcome law of the assigned energy observable is time-independent in every preparation, its finite moments are conserved, every bounded assigned sharp observable compatible with the energy has a time-independent outcome law, and a pure preparation is stationary exactly when it is an eigenray of the energy, in which case all its outcome laws are time-independent. No relaxation, equilibration or decay is asserted; no converse of the compatibility criterion is claimed for unbounded energy operators; no measurement, apparatus or empirical claim is made.

items.title: What the autonomous-dynamics page adopts, proves and does not claim
items.statement:
**What the page adopts.** The single physical assumption materialized here is the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), read in the vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for an isolated system of the framework with state space of the type fixed by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. In particular the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$, its energy unit and the reduced Planck constant entering the phase are model specifications in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; no numerical value of any of them is produced by this page.

**What is proved.** [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] draws, from P4 and the local mathematics [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]], the unitary flow, the invariance of the energy domain, the domain-qualified Schroedinger equation and the evolution of density-operator preparations. [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-picture]], using [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]], identifies the Heisenberg representative of a bounded assigned sharp observable and proves that the two pictures assign the same outcome laws, together with the domain-qualified Heisenberg equation and the freezing of energy-compatible bounded observables. [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] reads the conservation of the energy law and its finite moments, the conservation of any bounded energy-compatible observable, and the equivalence of stationary pure preparations with the eigenrays of the energy; the mathematical core of that equivalence is [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-ray-characterization]]. All statements are conditional consequences of the adopted postulates and the cited mathematics; none of them is an empirical claim.

**What is not claimed.** (i) The page treats only the autonomous case: a prescribed time-dependent family $t\mapsto H(t)$ and the propagator problems it raises are not covered by P4(ii) and are deferred to the driven-dynamics development, and an open or reduced non-unitary evolution is an extension requiring an environment model, in the sense of clauses (iv) and (v) of P4. (ii) No measurement, collapse, conditioning or apparatus model is introduced; the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] is used only to read statistics of a preparation, and the state after an outcome is not treated. (iii) No relaxation, equilibration or convergence of the law of a general preparation is asserted. (iv) The converse of the conservation criterion — that a bounded observable whose law is constant in every preparation must be strongly spectrally compatible with the energy — is not proved for a general possibly unbounded $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and is therefore not claimed. (v) The equation of motion is asserted exactly on the operator domain; for vectors outside the domain only the unitary flow, not the differential equation, is available.

**Empirical status.** Whether a concrete laboratory system realizes P4's isolated-system idealization, and whether a concrete apparatus realizes a preparation of the type used here, are tested identifications with uncertainty, in the sense of the framework's preparation and apparatus assumptions; they are not consequences of P4. This pair records no measurement, apparatus, calibration or data, and the worked companion page contains finite model computations only.
