items.title: Precession of a two-level preparation: exact phases, probabilities and a Bloch-vector rotation
items.statement:
Let $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ carry the standard inner product $\langle z,w\rangle=z_{1}\overline{w_{1}}+z_{2}\overline{w_{2}}$ ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]), with orthonormal basis $u_{1}=(1,0)$, $u_{2}=(0,1)$ and rank-one calculus $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Fix two distinct energies $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$ in joules (model parameters, not measured values), and consider the assigned energy observable of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (a),
$$H_{\mathrm{op}}:=E_{1}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+E_{2}T_{u_{2},u_{2}},\qquad u_{H}=\mathrm J,$$
of an isolated system whose state space is the two-level state space of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. Define the bounded self-adjoint observables
$$X:=T_{u_{1},u_{2}}+T_{u_{2},u_{1}},\qquad Y:=iT_{u_{2},u_{1}}-iT_{u_{1},u_{2}},\qquad Z:=T_{u_{1},u_{1}}-T_{u_{2},u_{2}},$$
with the same dimensionless unit, and let $\psi_{0}=\alpha u_{1}+\beta u_{2}$ be a unit vector. Writing
$$\omega:=\frac{E_{2}-E_{1}}{\hbar}\quad(\text{units }\mathrm s^{-1}),$$
the example establishes the following exact model statements.

(i) The spectral projection-valued measure of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is $E_{H}(B)=\mathbf 1_{E_{1}\in B}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+\mathbf 1_{E_{2}\in B}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$, and the flow is $U(t)=e^{-iE_{1}t/\hbar}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+e^{-iE_{2}t/\hbar}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$.

(ii) $X,Y,Z$ are bounded self-adjoint with $X^{2}=Y^{2}=Z^{2}=I$ and $XY=iZ$; their spectra are $\{\pm1\}$, with $Y$ and $Z$ obtained from $X$ by the same pattern.

(iii) The evolved preparation is $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi_{0}=\alpha e^{-iE_{1}t/\hbar}u_{1}+\beta e^{-iE_{2}t/\hbar}u_{2}$, of unit norm, and the expectations are
$$\langle X\rangle(t)=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\alpha\overline{\beta}\,e^{i\omega t}\bigr),\qquad \langle Y\rangle(t)=-2\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\alpha\overline{\beta}\,e^{i\omega t}\bigr),\qquad \langle Z\rangle(t)=|\alpha|^{2}-|\beta|^{2}.$$

(iv) The triple $v(t):=\bigl(\langle X\rangle(t),\langle Y\rangle(t),\langle Z\rangle(t)\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3}$ has constant norm one and is the rotation of $v(0)$ about the third axis by the angle $-\omega t$: $v(t)=R_{3}(-\omega t)v(0)$, where $R_{3}(\theta)(x,y,z)=(x\cos\theta-y\sin\theta,\ x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta,\ z)$. Thus the expectation-value triple precesses with angular frequency $\omega$.

(v) The outcome law of $X$ in the preparation $[\psi(t)]$ is the two-point law $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t)}(\{+1\})=(1+\langle X\rangle(t))/2$, $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t)}(\{-1\})=(1-\langle X\rangle(t))/2$; in particular for $\alpha=\beta=1/\sqrt{2}$ one has $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t)}(\{+1\})=(1+\cos\omega t)/2$.

(vi) The energy law is time-independent, $\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{1}\})=|\alpha|^{2}$ and $\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{2}\})=|\beta|^{2}$ for every $t$, and every one of the displayed expectations is periodic in $t$ with period $2\pi/|\omega|$ (when $\omega\ne0$, which holds because $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$).

The computation is a model-internal one: the energies are parameters of the assigned observable, the probabilities are those of the framework's outcome law, and no laboratory measurement, apparatus or empirical value is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with the standard inner product and orthonormal basis $(u_{1},u_{2})$; distinct real energies $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$ in joules, and the reduced Planck constant $\hbar$ with its value and unit, in the framework's quantity conventions ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]); the assigned energy observable $H_{\mathrm{op}}=E_{1}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+E_{2}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ with unit $\mathrm J$; the observables $X,Y,Z$; a unit vector $\psi_{0}=\alpha u_{1}+\beta u_{2}$; the number $\omega=(E_{2}-E_{1})/\hbar$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers.

[F1] **Rank-one calculus and one-dimensional projections.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is bounded with $T_{u,v}^{*}=T_{v,u}$, and the assignment is linear in $u$ and conjugate-linear in $v$; for every nonzero $\psi$ the operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ is self-adjoint positive trace class, and for every unit $u$ the operator $T_{u,u}$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto the one-dimensional subspace $\mathbb Cu$, so that $T_{u,u}$ is idempotent and $T_{u,u}\psi=\langle\psi,u\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]], [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Finite spectral structure.** For the bounded self-adjoint $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ with orthonormal eigenvectors $u_{1},u_{2}$ at the distinct eigenvalues $E_{1},E_{2}$, the assignment $E'(B):=\mathbf 1_{E_{1}\in B}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+\mathbf 1_{E_{2}\in B}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ takes orthogonal-projection values by [F1], satisfies $E'(\mathbb R)=I$ by [F7], and is additive and multiplicative over the two-point eigenvalue set, so it is a projection-valued measure; and $\int\lambda\,dE'(\lambda)=E_{1}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+E_{2}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}$; by the uniqueness of the spectral measure it is $E_{H}$ ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (a)).

[F7] **Resolution of the identity.** Since $(u_{1},u_{2})$ is an orthonormal basis of the two-dimensional space $H$, every $v\in H$ satisfies $v=\langle v,u_{1}\rangle u_{1}+\langle v,u_{2}\rangle u_{2}$, and therefore $T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+T_{u_{2},u_{2}}=I$ ([[thm-bessel-inequality-and-finite-parseval-identity]]).

[F3] **Bounded calculus for the two-point measure.** For bounded Borel $f$, $\Phi_{E_H}(f)=f(E_{1})T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+f(E_{2})T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$: the identity holds on the simple functions constant on the Borel partition $\{E_{1}\},\{E_{2}\},\mathbb R\setminus\{E_{1},E_{2}\}$ and passes to bounded Borel $f$ by uniform approximation ([[thm-pvm-integral-is-a-star-homomorphism]], [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

[F4] **Flow and state evolution.** The flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)=\Phi_{E_H}(e^{-it\lambda/\hbar})$ and the preparation evolves as $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi_{0}$, with $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi_{0}\|=1$; the energy law is time-independent ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (a), [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F5] **Outcome law.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A_{0},u_{A_{0}})$ the law of the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ is $\mu^{A_{0}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A_{0}}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, and the mean for a unit vector in $D(A_{0})$ is $\langle A_{0}\psi,\psi\rangle$; the law depends only on the ray ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b) and (e), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]).

[F6] **Complex exponential algebra.** For real $\theta,\phi$: $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$, $e^{i(\theta+\phi)}=e^{i\theta}e^{i\phi}$, $|e^{i\theta}|=1$ and $\overline{e^{i\theta}}=e^{-i\theta}$; for complex $z$, $2\operatorname{Re}z=z+\overline z$ and $2i\operatorname{Im}z=z-\overline z$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]], [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Moreover $\ker(\exp)=2\pi i\mathbb Z$, so for real $\theta$ one has $e^{i\theta}=1$ exactly for $\theta\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ ([[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the spectral measure, the flow, the algebra and the laws of the explicit two-dimensional model.

1.1 [Spectral measure and flow] $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is bounded and self-adjoint because $T_{u_{1},u_{1}},T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ are self-adjoint projections by [F1] and $E_{1},E_{2}\in\mathbb R$, and $H_{\mathrm{op}}u_{k}=E_{k}u_{k}$; on the two-point spectrum the assignment $E'$ of [F2] has orthogonal-projection values with $E'(\mathbb R)=I$ by [F7] and is additive and multiplicative, so [F2] identifies $E_{H}$, and [F3] with $f(\lambda)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}$ gives $U(t)=\sum_{k}e^{-iE_{k}t/\hbar}T_{u_{k},u_{k}}$. This is (i). [given, F1, F2, F3, F7, algebra]

1.2 [The three observables] By [F1] each of $X=T_{u_{1},u_{2}}+T_{u_{2},u_{1}}$, $Y=iT_{u_{2},u_{1}}-iT_{u_{1},u_{2}}$, $Z=T_{u_{1},u_{1}}-T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ is bounded and self-adjoint. Composing rank-one operators from their definition, $T_{u,v}T_{w,z}x=\langle\langle x,z\rangle w,v\rangle u=\langle w,v\rangle\langle x,z\rangle u$, so with orthonormality $T_{u_{1},u_{2}}T_{u_{2},u_{1}}=T_{u_{1},u_{1}}$, $T_{u_{2},u_{1}}T_{u_{1},u_{2}}=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ and all products of two distinct rank-one terms $T_{u_{j},u_{k}}T_{u_{l},u_{m}}$ with $k\ne l$ vanish; hence $X^{2}=T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+T_{u_{2},u_{2}}=I$ by [F1], $Y^{2}=I$, $Z^{2}=I$ and $XY=i(T_{u_{1},u_{1}}-T_{u_{2},u_{2}})=iZ$. The eigenvalues of $X$ are $\pm1$ with eigenvectors $e_{\pm}=(u_{1}\pm u_{2})/\sqrt2$, and $Y,Z$ obey the same pattern. This is (ii). [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 [Evolved preparation] By [F4] and step 1.1, $\psi(t)=\sum_{k}c_{k}e^{-iE_{k}t/\hbar}u_{k}$ with $c_{1}=\alpha$, $c_{2}=\beta$; all coefficients have modulus $|c_{k}|$ because $|e^{-iE_{k}t/\hbar}|=1$ by [F6], so $\|\psi(t)\|^{2}=|\alpha|^{2}+|\beta|^{2}=1$. This is the first assertion of (iii). [given, step 1.1, F4, F6, algebra]

3.1 [Expectations] With $\theta_{k}:=E_{k}t/\hbar$ and $\psi(t)=\alpha e^{-i\theta_{1}}u_{1}+\beta e^{-i\theta_{2}}u_{2}$, the actions $Xu_{1}=u_{2}$, $Xu_{2}=u_{1}$, $Yu_{1}=iu_{2}$, $Yu_{2}=-iu_{1}$, $Zu_{k}=\pm u_{k}$ from step 1.2 give $\langle X\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle=\alpha\overline{\beta}e^{i(\theta_{2}-\theta_{1})}+\overline{\alpha\beta e^{i(\theta_{2}-\theta_{1})}}=2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta}e^{i\omega t})$ and $\langle Y\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle=i\alpha\overline{\beta}e^{i(\theta_{2}-\theta_{1})}-i\overline{\alpha\beta e^{i(\theta_{2}-\theta_{1})}}=-2\operatorname{Im}(\alpha\overline{\beta}e^{i\omega t})$ and $\langle Z\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle=|\alpha|^{2}-|\beta|^{2}$, using $i(w-\overline w)=-2\operatorname{Im}w$ for $w=\alpha\overline{\beta}e^{i\omega t}$ and [F6]; by [F5] these are the means of $X,Y,Z$ in $[\psi(t)]$, which is (iii). [given, step 1.2, step 2.1, F5, F6, algebra]

4.1 [Precession of the triple] Write $c:=\alpha\overline{\beta}=re^{i\varphi}$ with $r\ge0$; then $v(t)=(2r\cos(\varphi+\omega t),\ -2r\sin(\varphi+\omega t),\ |\alpha|^{2}-|\beta|^{2})$ and $v(0)=(2r\cos\varphi,\ -2r\sin\varphi,\ |\alpha|^{2}-|\beta|^{2})$. The rotation formula $R_{3}(-\omega t)$ of the statement gives first coordinate $2r\cos\varphi\cos\omega t+2r\sin\varphi\sin\omega t=2r\cos(\varphi+\omega t)$ and second coordinate $-2r\cos\varphi\sin\omega t-2r\sin\varphi\cos\omega t=-2r\sin(\varphi+\omega t)$, matching the computed triple; its norm is $4r^{2}+(|\alpha|^{2}-|\beta|^{2})^{2}=4|\alpha|^{2}|\beta|^{2}+(|\alpha|^{2}+|\beta|^{2})^{2}-4|\alpha|^{2}|\beta|^{2}=1$ by [F6] and $|\alpha|^{2}+|\beta|^{2}=1$; this is (iv). [given, step 3.1, F6, algebra]

4.2 [Law of the flip observable] By step 1.2, $X=Q_{+}-Q_{-}$ with the orthogonal projections $Q_{\pm}=T_{e_{\pm},e_{\pm}}$ onto the eigenspaces of the eigenvalues $\pm1$, so $E_{X}(\{+1\})=Q_{+}$ and, by [F1], $Q_{+}\psi=\langle\psi,e_{+}\rangle e_{+}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\langle\psi,u_{1}\rangle+\langle\psi,u_{2}\rangle\bigr)e_{+}$. For $\psi=\psi(t)$ this gives $\|Q_{+}\psi(t)\|^{2}=\frac12\bigl|\alpha e^{-i\theta_{1}}+\beta e^{-i\theta_{2}}\bigr|^{2}=\frac12\bigl(1+\langle X\rangle(t)\bigr)$ by [F6] and step 3.1, and by [F5] this is $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t)}(\{+1\})$; the minus case is the complement, and for $\alpha=\beta=1/\sqrt2$ the value is $(1+\cos\omega t)/2$. This is (v). [given, step 1.2, step 3.1, F1, F5, F6, algebra]

4.3 [Energy law and periodicity] By [F4], $\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{k}\})=\|E_{H}(\{E_{k}\})\psi(t)\|^{2}=\|c_{k}e^{-iE_{k}t/\hbar}u_{k}\|^{2}=|c_{k}|^{2}$ using step 1.1 and [F6], so the two-point energy law is time-independent; all displayed functions are functions of $e^{i\omega t}$, and $e^{i\omega(t+2\pi/|\omega|)}=e^{i\omega t}$ because $\pm2\pi i\in\ker(\exp)$ by [F6], so they are periodic with period $2\pi/|\omega|$; here $\omega\ne0$ because $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$. This is (vi). [given, step 1.1, step 3.1, F4, F6, algebra]

5.1 Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 establish (i)-(vi) for the explicit model data. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 4.3] ∎

## Remarks

- **"Precession" is a bookkeeping device.** The rotation of $v(t)$ is a statement about three expectation values of three bounded observables of a two-level system; no rotating rigid body, magnetic moment or specific species is asserted. The frequency $\omega=(E_{2}-E_{1})/\hbar$ is fixed by the two energy parameters.
- **Relative versus global phase.** The evolution multiplies the two components by different phases; the relative phase $e^{i\omega t}$ is what moves the observables $X$ and $Y$, while a common phase of the whole vector would change no outcome law. For $\alpha=0$ or $\beta=0$ the preparation is an eigenray and the triple is constant, in agreement with the stationary-state theorem.
- **No detector is modeled.** The probabilities displayed are model outcome laws for the declared observables; no measurement interaction, resolution, efficiency or record is introduced.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 2.2, printed pages 21-23 (energy eigenstates acquire phases e^{-iEt/hbar}; general states evolve as finite superpositions with time-dependent relative phases)

The energies are model parameters; the item asserts no apparatus realization, no detection model and no empirical value, and it identifies the two-level system with no specific physical species.

items.title: A finite superposition of energy eigenrays: exact phases, laws and return times
items.statement:
Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be the state space of a declared isolated system of the framework ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be its assigned energy observable with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]), and let $u_{1},\dots,u_{N}$ be a finite orthonormal family of eigenvectors of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ with real eigenvalues $\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{N}$: $H_{\mathrm{op}}u_{n}=\lambda_{n}u_{n}$ for $n=1,\dots,N$. Fix coefficients $c_{n}\in\mathbb C$ and the nonzero vector
$$\psi_{0}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}c_{n}u_{n},\qquad S:=\{n:c_{n}\ne0\}.$$
Then, with $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi_{0}$:

(i) $\psi(t)=\sum_{n\in S}c_{n}e^{-i\lambda_{n}t/\hbar}u_{n}$ for every $t$, and $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$; if $S$ has one element, or more generally if all $\lambda_{n}$ with $n\in S$ coincide, the ray $[\psi(t)]$ is constant.

(ii) For every bounded assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the outcome law in the preparation $[\psi(t)]$ is
$$\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\sum_{m,n\in S}c_{n}\overline{c_{m}}\,e^{-i(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{m})t/\hbar}\,\langle E_{A}(B)u_{n},u_{m}\rangle .$$
Thus the probability is a finite trigonometric polynomial in $t$ with frequencies $(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{m})/\hbar$.

(iii) For $T>0$ the following are equivalent: (a) $[\psi(t+T)]=[\psi(t)]$ for every $t$; (b) $e^{-i\lambda_{n}T/\hbar}$ is independent of $n\in S$; (c) $(\lambda_{m}-\lambda_{n})T/\hbar\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for all $m,n\in S$.

(iv) Consequently a positive return time exists if and only if there are $\omega_{0}>0$ and integers $k_{n}$ ($n\in S$) with $(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{n_{0}})/\hbar=\omega_{0}k_{n}$ for all $n\in S$, where $n_{0}$ is any fixed element of $S$; and then $T=2\pi/\omega_{0}$ is a return time.

(v) Two-energy case $N=2$, $\lambda_{1}\ne\lambda_{2}$, $c_{1}c_{2}\ne0$: the positive return times are exactly $T=2\pi\hbar k/|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|$, $k=1,2,3,\dots$; the least return time is $2\pi\hbar/|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|$, which is the period $2\pi/|\omega|$ of the precession example with $\omega=(\lambda_{2}-\lambda_{1})/\hbar$.

(vi) In the stationary case of (i), every outcome law of every assigned sharp observable is independent of $t$: $\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)$.

The computation is a model-internal one: the eigenvalues are parameters of the assigned observable, and no identification with a physical spectrum, apparatus or measured value is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with flow $U(t)$; a finite orthonormal family $u_{1},\dots,u_{N}$ of eigenvectors with real eigenvalues $\lambda_{n}$; coefficients $c_{n}$ and the nonzero vector $\psi_{0}$; $S=\{n:c_{n}\ne0\}$; the evolved vectors $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi_{0}$; a bounded assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ with spectral measure $E_{A}$; a Borel set $B$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] **Eigenrays evolve by phases.** If $H_{\mathrm{op}}u=\lambda u$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, then $U(t)u=e^{-i\lambda t/\hbar}u$ for every $t$, and the flow is linear with $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$ ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clause (a), [[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conserved-spectral-probability-laws]] clause (d)).

[F2] **Outcome law for a pure preparation.** $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}=\langle E_{A}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ for a unit vector, and the number depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; the inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

[F3] **Complex exponential algebra.** For real $\theta,\phi$: $e^{i(\theta+\phi)}=e^{i\theta}e^{i\phi}$, $|e^{i\theta}|=1$ and $\overline{e^{i\theta}}=e^{-i\theta}$; for complex $z,w$, $\overline{zw}=\overline z\,\overline w$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]], [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Moreover $\ker(\exp)=2\pi i\mathbb Z$, so for real $\mu$ one has $e^{-i\mu}=1$ exactly for $\mu\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ ([[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]]).

[F4] **Orthonormality.** $\langle u_{n},u_{m}\rangle=\delta_{nm}$, and every $\psi_{0}$ as above is nonzero exactly when $S$ is nonempty ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; expand the evolved vector along the eigenfamily, evaluate the pairing term by term and read the return-time condition off the phases.

1.1 [Evolution of the superposition] By [F1] applied to each eigenvector, $U(t)u_{n}=e^{-i\lambda_{n}t/\hbar}u_{n}$; linearity of $U(t)$ gives $\psi(t)=\sum_{n=1}^{N}c_{n}e^{-i\lambda_{n}t/\hbar}u_{n}=\sum_{n\in S}c_{n}e^{-i\lambda_{n}t/\hbar}u_{n}$, and $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$ by the norm statement of [F1]. If all $\lambda_{n}$ with $n\in S$ equal a common $\lambda$, then $\psi(t)=e^{-i\lambda t/\hbar}\psi_{0}$, so $[\psi(t)]=[\psi_{0}]$ for every $t$. This is (i). [given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Trigonometric-polynomial law] Assume first $\|\psi_{0}\|=1$. By [F2] and step 1.1, using conjugate-linearity in the second argument, $\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\langle E_{A}(B)\sum_{n\in S}c_{n}e^{-i\lambda_{n}t/\hbar}u_{n},\sum_{m\in S}c_{m}e^{-i\lambda_{m}t/\hbar}u_{m}\rangle=\sum_{m,n\in S}c_{n}\overline{c_{m}}e^{-i(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{m})t/\hbar}\langle E_{A}(B)u_{n},u_{m}\rangle$, which is the display of (ii); for a general nonzero $\psi_{0}$ the same formula holds after dividing by $\|\psi_{0}\|^{2}$, since $\mu^{A}$ depends only on the ray by [F2]. [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.2 [Return-time criterion] Let $T>0$. If (a) holds, then for every $t$ there is $\zeta(t)\ne0$ with $\psi(t+T)=\zeta(t)\psi(t)$; pairing with $u_{m}$ for $m\in S$ and using orthonormality [F4] gives $c_{m}e^{-i\lambda_{m}(t+T)/\hbar}=\zeta(t)c_{m}e^{-i\lambda_{m}t/\hbar}$, hence $e^{-i\lambda_{m}T/\hbar}=\zeta(t)$ for every $m\in S$, which is (b). If (b) holds with common value $\zeta$, then $\psi(t+T)=\zeta\psi(t)$ by step 1.1, which is (a). Finally (b) holds exactly when $e^{-i(\lambda_{m}-\lambda_{n})T/\hbar}=1$ for all $m,n\in S$, and by the exponential kernel $\ker(\exp)=2\pi i\mathbb Z$ of [F3] this is exactly the integrality condition (c). This proves (iii). [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Common frequency and return time] Condition (iv) is the statement that the numbers $(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{n_{0}})/\hbar$ are integer multiples of one positive number $\omega_{0}$; by step 2.2 with $T=2\pi/\omega_{0}$ and [F3], $(\lambda_{m}-\lambda_{n})T/\hbar=2\pi(k_{m}-k_{n})\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for all $m,n\in S$, so $T$ is a return time. Conversely, if $T>0$ is a return time, then by step 2.2(c) applied with $m=n_{0}$ we have $(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{n_{0}})T/\hbar\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for all $n\in S$, that is $(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{n_{0}})/\hbar=\omega_{0}k_{n}$ with $\omega_{0}:=2\pi/T>0$ and integers $k_{n}$; this proves the equivalence of (iv). [given, step 2.2, F3, algebra]

3.2 [Two energies] Let $N=2$, $\lambda_{1}\ne\lambda_{2}$, $c_{1}c_{2}\ne0$ and $T>0$. By step 2.2(c) with $\{m,n\}=\{1,2\}$ the return times are exactly the solutions of $|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|T/\hbar\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, that is $T=2\pi\hbar k/|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|$ with $k\in\mathbb Z$, $k\ge1$; the least such $T$ is $2\pi\hbar/|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|=2\pi/|\omega|$ for $\omega=(\lambda_{2}-\lambda_{1})/\hbar$. This is (v). [given, step 2.2, algebra]

3.3 [Stationary case] If all $\lambda_{n}$, $n\in S$, equal a common $\lambda$, then by step 1.1 $\psi(t)=e^{-i\lambda t/\hbar}\psi_{0}$ and $[\psi(t)]=[\psi_{0}]$; by [F2] the outcome law of every bounded assigned sharp observable depends only on the ray, so $\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)$ for every $t$. This is (vi), and it agrees with the stationary-state characterization of [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c). [given, step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F2, algebra]

4.1 Steps 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 establish (i)-(vi) for the explicit model data. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 3.3] ∎

## Remarks

- **The relative phases are physical.** Only the relative phases $e^{-i(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{m})t/\hbar}$ appear in the laws; a common phase of $\psi(t)$ would not change any outcome law, in agreement with the ray reading of pure preparations.
- **Existence of a common frequency is a number-theoretic condition on the model data.** For two distinct energies it always holds, and the least return time is the inverse Bohr frequency of the precession example. For three or more energies it may fail, in which case the ray never returns to itself, although the laws remain finite sums of oscillations with the Bohr frequencies.
- **No detector is modeled.** Exactly as on the precession example, the probabilities displayed are model outcome laws; no measurement interaction, finite resolution, efficiency or record is introduced.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 2.3, printed pages 15-17 (the evolution operator for a time-independent Hamiltonian and its application to eigenstates)

items.physical_scope: A finite, exact model computation for a declared isolated system: the evolution of a nonzero finite superposition of orthogonal energy eigenrays, the resulting trigonometric-polynomial form of the outcome laws of bounded assigned sharp observables, the exact return-time criterion for the ray, the two-energy period, and the stationary case. The eigenvalues are model parameters; the item asserts no apparatus, no detection model and no empirical value, and no finite set of energies is identified with a physical spectrum.

items.title: A superposition of distinct energy eigenrays need not be stationary
items.statement:
Adopt the autonomous-dynamics reading of the framework ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics|P4]]). Then: **every** preparation of an isolated system that is a superposition of two or more energy eigenrays with distinct eigenvalues is a stationary state, in the sense that all of its outcome laws are independent of time; in particular a superposition of two eigenrays of the two-level model is stationary.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted autonomous-dynamics reading of the framework with the two-level model data of [[ex-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-two-level-precession]]: the Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{2}$, distinct energies $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$ in joules, the assigned energy observable $H_{\mathrm{op}}=E_{1}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+E_{2}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ with flow $U(t)$ and frequency $\omega=(E_{2}-E_{1})/\hbar\ne0$, the bounded self-adjoint flip observable $X=T_{u_{1},u_{2}}+T_{u_{2},u_{1}}$, and the unit vector $\psi_{0}=(u_{1}+u_{2})/\sqrt2$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] **The model data and the law of $X$.** In the two-level model, $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi_{0}=\alpha e^{-iE_{1}t/\hbar}u_{1}+\beta e^{-iE_{2}t/\hbar}u_{2}$ for unit $\psi_{0}=\alpha u_{1}+\beta u_{2}$, $\langle X\rangle(t)=2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta}e^{i\omega t})$, and $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t)}(\{+1\})=(1+\langle X\rangle(t))/2$ ([[ex-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-two-level-precession]] clauses (i), (iii) and (v)).

[F2] **Stationary states are the eigenrays.** A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, that is $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, exactly when $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$; for a non-eigenvector the ray is not constant ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c)).

[F3] **Trigonometric values.** For real $x$ one has $\cos(x+\pi)=-\cos x$ and $\cos(-x)=\cos x$; in particular $\cos\pi=-1$ and $\cos(-\pi)=-1$ ([[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]).

[F4] **Euler form of the phase.** $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ for real $\theta$, so $2\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\theta})=2\cos\theta$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]]). Moreover $\ker(\exp)=2\pi i\mathbb Z$, so for real $\theta$ one has $e^{i\theta}=1$ exactly for $\theta\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ ([[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]]).

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the outcome law of the flip observable of the two-level model at two times and show that it takes different values.

1.1 [The preparation and its frequency] The vector $\psi_{0}=(u_{1}+u_{2})/\sqrt2$ is a unit vector with $\alpha=\beta=1/\sqrt2$, so $\alpha\overline{\beta}=1/2$ and, by [F1], $\langle X\rangle(t)=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\frac12e^{i\omega t}\bigr)=\cos\omega t$ by [F4], with $\omega=(E_{2}-E_{1})/\hbar\ne0$ because $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$. [given, F1, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Two values of the law] At $t=0$ one has $e^{i\omega\cdot0}=1$ since $0\in\ker(\exp)$ by [F4], so $\langle X\rangle(0)=2\operatorname{Re}(1/2)=1$ by step 1.1 and the law of $X$ in $[\psi_{0}]$ is $\mu^{X}_{\psi_{0}}(\{+1\})=(1+1)/2=1$. At $t_{0}:=\pi/|\omega|>0$ one has $\omega t_{0}=\pm\pi$, so $\cos(\omega t_{0})=\cos(\pm\pi)=-1$ by [F3], and therefore $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t_{0})}(\{+1\})=(1-1)/2=0$. [given, step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [The claim fails] The outcome law of the bounded assigned sharp observable $X$ takes the value $1$ at $t=0$ and the value $0$ at $t=t_{0}>0$ in the same preparation $[\psi_{0}]$; hence this law is not independent of time and the superposition $[\psi_{0}]$ is not stationary. By [F2] this is exactly as it must be, since $\psi_{0}$ is not an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$: $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi_{0}=(E_{1}u_{1}+E_{2}u_{2})/\sqrt2$ is a multiple of $\psi_{0}=(u_{1}+u_{2})/\sqrt2$ only if $E_{1}=E_{2}$. This refutes the displayed universal claim. [given, step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What is not refuted.** Each eigenray is stationary by [F2], and a superposition whose nonzero coefficients all carry the same eigenvalue is stationary too; the refuted assertion is the universal one about superpositions of *distinct* eigenvalues. The failure is produced by the relative phase $e^{i\omega t}$, not by any external disturbance.
- **The two-times computation is exact model arithmetic.** Both probabilities are consequences of the framework's outcome law for the declared finite model; no detector, efficiency, resolution or recorded data is involved.

items.physical_scope: A refutation, inside the framework's autonomous-dynamics reading, of the informal claim that every superposition of two or more distinct energy eigenrays of an isolated system is a stationary state with time-independent outcome laws: in the explicit two-level model with two distinct energies, an equal-weight superposition carries the bounded flip observable with an outcome probability oscillating between one and zero. The item refutes that specific universal claim; it asserts no apparatus, no measurement statistics from a laboratory and no empirical result, and it does not deny that individual eigenrays are stationary or that special superpositions can be stationary.

items.title: What the worked items of the companion page establish
items.statement:
**Two-level precession.** [[ex-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-two-level-precession]] computes, on the explicit two-dimensional state space, the spectral measure and flow of the assigned energy observable $E_{1}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+E_{2}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ with $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$, the exact phases of an evolved preparation, the outcome probabilities and expectations of three bounded observables, and the rotation of the expectation-value triple about the third axis with angular frequency $\omega=(E_{2}-E_{1})/\hbar$. The computation verifies the flow and law of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] on finite data, and it confirms the energy conservation of [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (a) in the model. No apparatus realization, detector resolution or measured frequency is asserted.

**Finite superpositions.** [[ex-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-finite-stationary-superposition]] computes the evolution of a nonzero finite superposition of orthogonal energy eigenrays, the trigonometric-polynomial form of the outcome laws of a bounded assigned sharp observable, the exact return-time criterion $(\lambda_{m}-\lambda_{n})T/\hbar\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for $m,n$ in the support of the coefficients, the existence criterion for a positive return time via a common frequency, and the two-energy specialization with least return time $2\pi\hbar/|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|$. These are exact model statements under the flow of [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]].

**A failed universal claim.** [[cex-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-superposition-with-distinct-energies-is-not-stationary]] refutes the informal universal statement that every superposition of distinct energy eigenrays is stationary: on the two-level model with $\psi_{0}=(u_{1}+u_{2})/\sqrt2$ the outcome law of the flip observable takes the values $1$ at $t=0$ and $0$ at $t=\pi/|\omega|$. The refutation isolates the relative phase as the mechanism and is consistent with the exact stationarity criterion of [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c): the individual eigenrays are stationary, the equal-weight superposition of distinct eigenrays is not.

## What the page does not establish

None of the three items is an experiment: no counts, calibration, resolution, efficiency, background, uncertainty or data comparison appears anywhere on the page, and no energy value is measured. The two-level system is an abstract model and is not identified with a spin, a magnetic moment, a photon polarization or any other species; the coupling of spin to a magnetic field belongs to the corresponding model pages, and driven or resonant dynamics is deferred to the driven-dynamics development, which adopts its own time-dependent assumptions. The return-time and precession results are statements about the model's flow and outcome law, not about the stability, decoherence or control of any laboratory preparation.
